Proposed evaluation plan (short):

- 2-week eval sprint: functional + perf; Redwood runs smoke tests and a 1-hour production-like load test mid-sprint.
- Post-sprint acceptance: joint sign-off on a 6-item checklist (API stability, latency SLA, cost per 1M tokens, KV cache hit rate, long-token behavior, failure/retry behavior).

On lead times: Ben, can you confirm how much runway we need to guarantee the H100 tranche vs. fallbacks? Neha/Marissa — I'm adding a few gating milestones into the MAP and will attach a DocuSign request for the initial MSA/LOI if Helix is comfortable.

Best,
Chloe Martin

Chloe/Team — quick technical sizing notes and options so procurement has something concrete to weigh.

Summary assumptions pulled from Helix footprint: 8 prod endpoints, 3 batch jobs, median seq len 512, peak concurrency 120 QPS.

Option A (H100 primary):
- Start: reserve 8 H100s (mixed 80/90GB) to hit p95 < 180ms for gen workload with batching and KV cache.
- Ramp: +12 H100s across 8 weeks for throughput headroom.
- Lead time: 16–20 weeks from PO to dedicated pool activation (vendor dependent).

Option B (Mixed quantized fallback):
- Reserve 12 A2-type nodes with int8/4q variants for a lower-cost baseline. p95 ~ 230–320ms depending on quant profile; lower throughput per device but far shorter lead time (2–4 weeks).

Operational notes:
- We can recommend a staged roll: start with mixed quantized Dedicated capacity to get traffic onto Redwood and validate the MAP while H100s are provisioning. At commit, we convert the pool and migrate with rolling traffic shift.
- Acceptance criteria: provide a 6-point checklist (I will draft) — must include a reproducible load-test command and a fixed seed prompt set for quality regression checks.

Link: internal sizing doc (drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/sizing/RDW-2027-0387 (Helix has view-only)

-Ben
